findings.where: Hero, the action row under the second paragraph (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: The row has two solid blue buttons that look the same, 'Write to me' and 'Book a consultation', with the email address set between them. Because they look alike (similarity), neither one reads as the main action. Because the address sits close to both (proximity), it is unclear which button it belongs to. The first screen asks for two things where it should ask for one.
findings.who_objects: A development-bank officer ready to get in touch has to stop and choose between two equal routes, and can't tell whether the address belongs to writing or to booking. The founder would object too: the brief asks for one message and one direct, personal way to reach Mark, and a 'Book a consultation' button sitting level with it reads like a firm's sales funnel.

findings.where: Phone hero, the action stack at the foot of the hero band
findings.fault: The stack breaks apart. 'Write to me' sits on the left edge, the address wraps under it, and 'Book a consultation' is pushed about 16 px in from the left edge, jammed under the address with almost no gap. The three items share no left edge or even spacing, so they look like a layout accident, not a designed group.
findings.who_objects: A phone visitor at the moment of contact sees a ragged, crowded cluster, and the page looks unfinished at the one place it has to look sure of itself. Most of this audience reads on the move and will first meet the page on a phone.

findings.fault: On a phone the hero stacks everything in one column: heading, a margin note, the photo and its caption, the four-line capitals paragraph, another note, the second paragraph, a third note, then the action. The way to reach Mark only comes up near the end of the second screen, about 1,400 px down. Nothing about contact shows on the first phone screen.
findings.who_objects: A phone visitor who decides early to get in touch has to scroll through two screens of mixed small and large blocks to find how. The brief asks for one message and one action on the first screen.

findings.where: Motion sketch section (desktop), the replay photo and the timing table in the right column
findings.fault: The two columns don't line up. The replay photo starts far below the section heading and is centred over the table instead of sitting on its left edge, which is where 'Replay the entrance' starts. Under the curve, the left column is empty for about 450 px while the right column carries the photo, link and table. The table is held to about half the page width, so '120 ms', '900 ms' and 'Exhibit photo' wrap onto two lines even though there is room to spare.
findings.who_objects: The founder judges these specimen parts as part of the candidate. Here the section looks like leftover pieces, not a set page, which works against the 'well-set brief' this direction promises.

findings.where: Header (desktop), the logo lockup against the header band
findings.fault: The 'MMM INFRA' lettering under the arches sits only a few pixels above the header band's bottom edge, so it looks pressed against the line where the band meets the hero. The nav also aligns with nothing in the lockup: its baseline is below the name and above the subtitle.
findings.who_objects: A careful eye, such as the founder's or Mark's, would see the logo, the one fixed brand element, crammed against an edge on a page whose whole lever is careful setting.
